title: Private School Admin Office Rates: Faculty Wing Crew Costs and Restroom Pricing Breakdown
seoTitle: Private School Admin Office Rates: Faculty Wing Cleaning Cost Guide
metaDescription: Private school admin office rates: a 12,000 sq ft faculty wing cleaned nightly runs about $18,970-$33,080 a month. Model your wing in our cleaning calculator.
excerpt: Private school administrative suites and faculty wings combine office-style cleaning with school-grade traffic, parent visitors, and an academic calendar that changes service needs every summer. This breakdown shows per-sq-ft rates, restroom pricing, and how business managers can budget nightly service during the year and lighter service over breaks.
quickAnswer: Private school admin offices and faculty wings of 10,000-24,999 sq ft are typically quoted at $0.07-$0.12 per sq ft per visit plus $15-$30 per restroom, and smaller 2,500-9,999 sq ft admin suites at $0.09-$0.15. A 12,000 sq ft VCT faculty wing with six restrooms cleaned five nights a week runs roughly $18,970-$33,080 per month during the school year, dropping to about $4,475-$7,785 per month on a once-weekly summer schedule.

blocks.text: What Makes a Private School Admin Wing Different From a Standard Office

A private school's administrative and faculty wing looks like an office on a floor plan: a head of school suite, admissions and advancement offices, a business office, a registrar, faculty workrooms, and a lounge. In practice it absorbs far more traffic. Parents arrive for tours and conferences, students visit the front desk and attendance office, faculty move between classrooms and workrooms all day, and evening events bring prospective families through the lobby. Restroom fixtures serve staff and guests, the faculty lounge functions as a busy commercial kitchenette, and the entry floors take on grit tracked in from playing fields and parking lots.

That profile is why most schools clean admin and faculty space five nights a week during the academic year, and why the restroom and flooring lines in a proposal deserve as much scrutiny as the per-square-foot rate. It also explains why the summer months offer the clearest savings opportunity in the entire contract.
Benchmark Rates for Private School Admin and Faculty Wings

The scenarios below use national benchmark brackets: $0.09-$0.15 per sq ft per visit for 2,500-9,999 sq ft, $0.07-$0.12 for 10,000-24,999 sq ft, and $0.05-$0.10 for 25,000 sq ft and larger. Frequency multipliers are 0.90 for five nights a week, 0.95 for three times weekly, and 1.08 for weekly service. VCT flooring adds a 1.04 multiplier and mixed carpet and hard floors 1.05. Restrooms are priced at $15-$30 each per visit, and monthly totals use 4.33 weeks per month.

blocks.title: Budget by the academic calendar, not 12 equal months
blocks.text: Ten school-year months at five nights a week plus two summer months at once weekly put the 12,000 sq ft wing at about $198,660-$346,350 per year, compared with $227,650-$396,940 if nightly service ran all twelve months. That is a potential savings of roughly $29,000-$50,600 without touching scope during the school year.
Restroom Density and Pricing in Faculty Wings

Admin and faculty wings usually carry a higher restroom-to-square-foot ratio than commercial offices because building codes and school design place restrooms near the front office for visitors and near faculty workrooms for staff who have limited breaks between classes. A 12,000 sq ft wing with six restrooms carries $90-$180 per visit in restroom charges alone, which is $1,949-$3,897 per month at five nights a week. That is often 10-12% of the entire contract.

items: Separate staff-only and visitor restrooms on the bid sheet; visitor restrooms near the lobby see heavier use during admissions season and events.
Ask whether a nurse's office restroom inside the admin wing is included, since it may require bloodborne-pathogen-trained cleaning.
Confirm restocking responsibility and par levels; faculty restrooms that run out of paper mid-day generate complaints out of proportion to their cost.
Request a midday restroom check during heavy event weeks as a priced add-on rather than an open-ended favor.

blocks.text: Traffic Wear: Entries, Corridors, and the Faculty Lounge

Floor wear in a school admin wing concentrates in three places. The main entry and reception lobby collect sand, mulch, and athletic-field grit, which abrades carpet and dulls VCT finish within weeks if walk-off matting and nightly vacuuming are neglected. Corridors connecting the admin wing to classrooms see dense pass-through traffic at bell times. The faculty lounge, with its refrigerators, coffee makers, and shared lunch tables, generates spills and food debris that demand nightly damp-mopping and sanitation.

Vacuum selection directly affects labor minutes. Corded 10-quart backpacks such as the ProTeam Super Coach Pro 10, with four-level HEPA filtration, a 12.5 lb harness weight, and a 66 dBA sound level, and the Sanitaire SC412A, with sealed HEPA filtration, a 10 qt capacity, 11.5 lb weight, and 68 dBA rating, both cover carpeted offices and lobby areas fast while trapping fine dust. In long corridors and during early-evening service when faculty are still working, the cordless Hoover Commercial MPWR 40V backpack, with a 6 qt capacity, HEPA media, and 14 lb weight, eliminates cord hazards and outlet hunting. Ask vendors which units they assign to your building and how they handle filter changes.
Recommended Frequency Through the School Year

items.name: Academic year: five nights a week
items.text: Trash, restrooms, lounge sanitation, high-touch disinfection, and traffic-lane vacuuming every night, with full detail vacuuming and dusting rotated through the week.

items.name: Admissions and event season: add event coverage
items.text: Price a post-event lobby and restroom reset for open houses, parent nights, and graduation rather than relying on the next regular visit.

items.name: Winter and spring breaks: three visits a week or fewer
items.text: With faculty mostly absent, reduce to 3x/week or 1x/week and schedule deep work such as carpet extraction while rooms are empty.

items.name: Summer: weekly service plus project work
items.text: Drop to weekly routine cleaning for the skeleton admin staff and schedule VCT strip-and-refinish and full carpet extraction as separately priced projects.

blocks.title: Lock calendar adjustments into the contract
blocks.text: Write the school calendar into the agreement with specific reduced frequencies for each break, and require the vendor to reflect those adjustments on the invoice automatically. Contracts that rely on verbal notice often bill nightly service through July.

faqs.q: Why are private school admin offices more expensive to clean than corporate offices of the same size?
faqs.a: They usually require five-night service, carry more restrooms per square foot, and see visitor, student, and event traffic that wears floors faster. The per-square-foot rate is often similar, but higher frequency and restroom counts raise the monthly total. Vetting and badging requirements for school contractors can add a further few percent.

faqs.q: How should we budget cleaning across summer and school breaks?
faqs.a: Price the school-year months at full frequency and the break months at reduced frequency, then add separately priced projects such as floor refinishing. Using 4.33 weeks per month, a 12,000 sq ft wing drops from roughly $18,970-$33,080 per month at five nights to about $4,475-$7,785 at once weekly.

faqs.q: Should the faculty lounge be priced as a breakroom add-on?
faqs.a: Yes. Breakroom and kitchenette sanitation typically runs $12-$25 per visit, covering counters, sinks, microwave interiors, refrigerator exteriors, and cabinet pulls. Busy faculty lounges with multiple refrigerators or a dishwasher may warrant the upper end. Clarify whether cleaning out refrigerators is included and how often.

faqs.q: What insurance should a school require from its cleaning contractor?
faqs.a: Require a certificate of insurance with general liability, commonly $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate, workers' compensation at statutory limits, auto liability, and a janitorial bond. Many schools also require sexual abuse and molestation coverage and name the school as additional insured. Verify certificates with the issuing agent annually.

faqs.q: Which tasks are commonly excluded from admin wing cleaning bids?
faqs.a: VCT stripping and refinishing, carpet extraction, exterior and high interior windows, cleaning inside classrooms outside the defined wing, post-event setup and teardown of furniture, and biohazard response are typical exclusions. Each should appear as a separately priced line so the business office can schedule and approve it.
